A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-driven dataset-distillation study. All pages, including equations, tables, plots and image-only appendices, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification results, cross-architecture evaluations, resource measurements and ablations in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v4 reports original classification and ablation results, including additional hard-label evaluations and cumulative synthesis-time measurements.

M1.justification: The patch-selection, DIFT clustering, ranking and patch-assembly pipeline remains. However, v4 Algorithm 1 and Equations 4–6 replace loss differences L_t with noise-map differences N_t, while the abstract and ablation discussion still describe loss differences. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or reflects inconsistent notation. Pooling itself was already described in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification using CIFAR-10/100, TinyImageNet, ImageNette, ImageWoof, ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1K. The added hard-label experiment and 10/20-class timing cases change supervision and subset configurations within retained ImageNet coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds IGD, D3HR and MGD3. Table 2 replaces D4M with RDED in the ConvNet comparison and RDED with D4M in the ResNet-18 comparison. The new hard-label comparison includes Random, while v2's cross-method ResNet-101 comparison is removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include one-hot-label evaluation at IPC 1/10/50/100 and individual/cumulative timing for 10/20-class ImageNet subsets at IPC 100/200. These replace the earlier per-image timing and GPU-memory comparison at IPC 50. v4 also changes the reported DIFT timestep from 1.60 to 0.16 in Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.1, although Section 4.5 retains 1.60; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a substantive test of dataset quality without teacher soft labels, and Figure 5 tests computational reuse across configurations. Conversely, v2 Table 1's systematic concatenated-versus-single-patch comparison disappears. The t-SNE, timestep, cluster-count and resizing analyses largely persist; their relocation is not an addition.

E5.justification: Both versions specify evaluation using five randomly initialized networks and report averages with ± values in accuracy tables. No new run-count, seed, uncertainty-definition, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is documented.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation entries change. For ImageNet-1K at IPC 50, Table 1 reports 59.4±0.2 for v2 OursS versus 61.0±0.3 for v4 Ours. The ResNet-18-teacher/ViT-B result changes from 69.2 to 63.7. New hard-label results include 10.5±0.3 at IPC 10, below RDED's 11.4±0.4. Timing results are replaced and several sensitivity curves change. These are reporting differences, not established same-procedure performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 revises the formal scoring expressions in Equations 4–6 and explicitly defines the spatial map and patch sum in Equations 6–7. Equivalence to v2's loss-based expressions is unresolved because N_t is separately defined as forward corruption in Equation 1. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diffusion-guided selection instead of generation, clustering for representative and diverse samples, reusable one-step distillation, and strong large-scale and cross-architecture performance. Retitling and revised wording do not establish a distinct new core claim.

C2.justification: The new hard-label discussion attributes baseline weaknesses to insufficient diversity and image-label misalignment. v2's detailed explanations for patch composition and soft-label calibration, plus some t-SNE interpretations, are shortened or removed. The central diversity–representativeness explanation and small-sample ViT limitation remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies interpolation from latent to image resolution and channel averaging before patch scoring. It removes the explicit FKD identification and KL training-objective description while retaining teacher-provided soft labels. Hardware and basic preprocessing remain documented, but the conflicting 0.16/1.60 timestep statements make implementation guidance less consistent.

R1.justification: The discussion is substantially refocused toward model-finetuned and prototype-finetuned diffusion families, adding IGD, MGD3 and D3HR references. The earlier overview of kernel, gradient, feature and trajectory matching is removed, together with several corresponding references. The overarching positioning of selection against diffusion-based generation remains.

P1.justification: Beyond the rewritten title and abstract, v4 substantially reorganizes existing material: diffusion preliminaries move into related work, experimental settings move to Appendix A.1, and qualitative and timestep analyses move into the main text. Method subsections are consolidated, and the supplement is reorganized into sections A–C.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and Table 1 is reorganized by model family, removing separate patch-variant and ResNet-101 blocks. v4 adds a timing plot and hard-label table, removes the resource table and two patch illustrations, and relocates/resizes several analyses. The large appendix image grids are retained rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: Newer baselines, hard-label evaluation and cumulative timing strengthen empirical validation. However, v4 removes direct patch-composition and ResNet-101 baseline comparisons and explicit FKD details, while introducing unresolved scoring and timestep inconsistencies. Reported default results also diverge without explanation: ImageNet-1K IPC-100 accuracy is 63.0 in Table 1 versus 63.4 in Table 5, whereas v2 reports 61.8 in both. These gains and losses in evidence and traceability prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
